title: Improve streaming disconnect errors (request ID propagation + clearer classification)
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: Support escalations around streaming resets/truncation (notably us-east) have been slowed by ambiguous client-visible errors and missing request IDs in some disconnect paths. This PR improves server-side error classification for streaming disconnects and ensures request ID propagation is consistent across gateway -> runtime -> client responses/logs. The goal is to let Support quickly distinguish (a) client/proxy disconnects, (b) upstream runtime cancellations, and (c) internal gateway timeouts, and to reliably hand customers a request_id they can paste back into tickets. Changes: (1) Introduce a dedicated StreamingDisconnect error category with stable public error codes and safe-to-share messaging. (2) Guarantee request_id inclusion in error payloads for streaming responses (including mid-stream termination) and in trailing metadata where applicable. (3) Improve logging: emit a single structured log line on stream termination with reason enum + timing + bytes/tokens sent (no customer payload). (4) Normalize mapping between internal cancellation reasons and public-facing error codes to reduce misclassification as 500. Notes: No customer-specific details in messages; wording reviewed with Support/CS expectations. Follow-ups: docs/SDK troubleshooting updates are tracked separately (see redwood-docs PRs).
commits: gateway: add streaming disconnect reason enum + mapping to public error codes
gateway: propagate request_id into streaming error frames + trailers
runtime-client: normalize cancellation reason translation (client disconnect vs upstream cancel)
obs: add structured termination log + metrics tag (disconnect_reason)
tests: add integration coverage for mid-stream disconnect paths
implementation_notes: Public error schema impact: This keeps the existing top-level error shape, but adds/guarantees the following fields on streaming termination errors: error.code (string, stable), error.message (string, customer-safe), and request_id (string). The request_id is already present for most JSON errors; the missing gap was mid-stream termination where we were not reliably attaching metadata. We now (a) set x-redwood-request-id header early in the stream, and (b) include request_id in the final error frame when we emit a structured error event. Classification: We add StreamingDisconnectReason with values CLIENT_CLOSED, UPSTREAM_CANCELLED, GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, INTERNAL_RESET, UNKNOWN. Mapping rules: CLIENT_CLOSED -> code=stream.disconnected_client (HTTP 499 semantics but still surfaced as streaming error frame), UPSTREAM_CANCELLED -> stream.cancelled_upstream, GATEWAY_TIMEOUT -> stream.timeout_gateway, INTERNAL_RESET -> stream.reset_internal, UNKNOWN -> stream.disconnected_unknown. We also ensure we do not surface raw Node/Envoy error strings to customers. Observability: Adds metric tag disconnect_reason on gateway_stream_terminated_total and logs a single event stream.termination with request_id, disconnect_reason, time_to_first_token_ms, total_duration_ms, bytes_sent, tokens_sent_estimate (if available).
testing: Unit: services/gateway (stream_errors + mapping) Integration: added cases for (1) client disconnect before first token, (2) client disconnect mid-stream, (3) upstream cancellation mid-stream, (4) gateway idle timeout. Validated that request_id is present in headers for all streaming responses and present in termination error frame when applicable. Verified no customer prompt/completion content is logged.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge to main 2) Deploy to canary gateway in us-east and eu-west 3) Monitor: gateway_stream_terminated_total by disconnect_reason, rate of 5xx vs streaming termination errors, and Support-reported ability to find request IDs 4) If no regression after 2 hours, roll to all regions. If regression: revert commit set (safe, no schema migrations).
release_notes: Gateway now classifies streaming disconnects with stable error codes and consistently includes request_id in streaming termination errors to speed triage.
conversation: Rafael Mendes (SRE): Can we avoid calling these 500s? Support is seeing generic 500 and paging SRE prematurely. Also, please confirm request_id is present even when the stream ends early. Ethan Park (author): Yep—this PR stops mapping disconnects to 500. We emit a streaming error frame with stable code and message, and we always set x-redwood-request-id header at stream start. Early-termination cases now also include request_id in the error frame if we have to send one. Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please make sure logs are a single structured event; we don’t want multiple lines per stream end. Also ensure we do not log customer content. Ethan Park: Updated to emit a single stream.termination event with reason + timings, no payload. Added a test asserting message strings do not include raw socket errors. Mina Haddad (Routing/Platform): For UPSTREAM_CANCELLED: can we distinguish fallback-induced cancel vs capacity cancel? Might help Support during incidents. Ethan Park: Not in this PR; we only have the coarse cancellation reason at this layer. I added a TODO and linked ENG-4821 for richer routing/fallback signals. Allison Grant (Observability): Metric tag cardinality OK, but please keep enum small and documented. Ethan Park: Kept enum to 5 values; added runbook note and metric docs line. Rafael Mendes: Request changes: add an integration test for mid-stream disconnect + verify request_id is visible to client. Ethan Park: Added integration test stream_disconnects.test.ts (client close mid-stream) verifying header and error frame includes request_id. Rafael Mendes: Approved. Sean Gallagher: Approved after last push. Merge: Squash merge by Ethan Park; auto-deploy scheduled via release train.
ci_summary: Checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass), lint (pass), typecheck (pass). One transient integration failure on first run (flaky timing) resolved by increasing disconnect wait threshold in test from 50ms->150ms; rerun passed.
security_considerations: Customer-safe messaging only; no raw socket/proxy error strings exposed. No customer content logged. Request IDs are already considered support-safe identifiers and are routinely shared by customers during escalations.
